Building in Brandon or Riverview: Check the Lot First

By Unique Building Contractors · October 23, 2026

The short answer

Before building in Brandon or Riverview, investigate the parcel rather than relying on lot size or a listing description. Confirm legal and physical access, survey information, utilities, drainage questions and the permitting authority. Use the findings to define a buildable concept and a transparent site-work budget.

Turn the property information into a feasibility brief

Collect the parcel identifier, survey, available title information and any existing improvement records. Ask the design team to identify information that is missing or needs updating. A boundary drawing, a listing sketch and a construction site plan serve different purposes; clarify which documents the next design decision requires.

In Brandon, Riverview and nearby Valrico, use local place names to describe location, not to infer a uniform set of site conditions. Two parcels nearby can differ in access, recorded restrictions and utility arrangements. Record findings for the specific address and keep unresolved assumptions visible.

Confirm utilities and the route to the building area

Ask how water, wastewater, electrical service and other required connections will reach the proposed building. Identify who verifies availability, capacity and connection scope. If a septic system is part of the proposal, discuss the required project-specific documentation before finalizing the layout.

Walk the intended delivery route with the project team. Consider equipment access, overhead obstructions, turning room and material storage. Define whether temporary access work or restoration is included. A lot can fit a house on paper while still needing a detailed plan for constructing it.

Resolve drainage and foundation questions before pricing certainty

Ask the relevant professionals what site, soil and elevation information they need. Discuss how the proposed home, driveway and outdoor surfaces interact with drainage. A dry visit to the site does not establish how it behaves during heavy rain, and nearby construction does not establish the correct foundation for your parcel.

Request a list of investigations and the design decisions each one supports. The goal is to replace assumptions with usable information before committing to dependent work. Do not treat a generic foundation or grading allowance as confirmation that the actual site design is complete.

Compare proposals with a shared scope sheet

Give each builder the same available documents and ask for a breakdown of building work, site preparation, utility connections, allowances and exclusions. Identify who carries the cost of additional investigation or a change in the site design. Keep contingency distinct from money already assigned to known work.

Hillsborough County provides residential checklists and addition submission guidance. Confirm which current checklist applies to the actual project and who will coordinate responses to review comments. Build a schedule that includes missing information, approvals, procurement and inspections before expecting a reliable start date.

Your planning checklist

  • Gather parcel, survey and available property records.
  • Confirm jurisdiction and project submission requirements.
  • Investigate access and utility connections.
  • Assign drainage, soil and foundation questions.
  • Compare bids using one scope and allowance sheet.

Common questions

Is the cheapest lot the cheapest place to build in Riverview?

The purchase price is only one part of the project. Access, utilities, site preparation, design requirements and other parcel conditions can change the overall cost. Compare total project assumptions before choosing.

What should I bring to a Brandon new-construction consultation?

Bring the parcel address, available survey and records, a room-use brief, your target budget and any purchase or planning deadlines. List unknowns so the team can propose the next investigations.
